skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray with a diffuse reticulonodular pattern to distinguish between interstitial lung disease, Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH), and heart failure.
steps: Assess the distribution of the reticulonodular opacities: determine if they are diffuse throughout all lung zones or restricted to specific areas (e.g., upper/mid zones with basal sparing).
Evaluate the costophrenic angles and lung bases for blunting or opacity indicating pleural effusion.
Check the cardiac silhouette size and pulmonary vasculature for signs of cardiomegaly or cephalization.

Differentiate based on combinations: Diffuse pattern + pleural effusion suggests interstitial lung disease; Upper/mid zone predominance + spared costophrenic angles suggests LCH; Cardiomegaly + vascular redistribution suggests heart failure.

skills.trigger: When identifying the specific zonal distribution of parenchymal lung disease on a chest radiograph.
steps: Visually divide the lungs into upper, middle, and lower zones using anatomical landmarks (rib levels, hilum).
Compare the density and prominence of reticular or nodular markings across these zones.
Specifically inspect the costophrenic recesses to confirm presence or absence of disease/effusion in the extreme lower fields.
Map the findings to characteristic patterns: basilar predominance (fibrosis/edema), apical/mid-zone predominance (LCH/sarcoid/TB), or uniform diffuse involvement.
